'''Xu Xiaobai''' (May 28, 1927 – March 27, 2014), [[Suzhou]], [[Jiangsu]], environmental chemist, inorganic chemist, academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" />

== Biography ==
Xu Xiaobai studied at Shanghai [[Nanyang Model High School|Nanyang Model Middle School]] in her early years. She graduated from the Department of Chemistry of [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University|Shanghai Jiaotong University]] in 1948. After that, she went to work at the department of chemistry of [[Academia Sinica]] as a student of chemist [[:zh:梁树权|Liang Shuquan]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.rcees.cas.cn/zxjs/yszl/201112/t20111212_3411320.html|title=徐晓白院士----中国科学院生态研究中心|website=www.rcees.cas.cn|access-date=2020-04-04|archive-date=2020-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407052435/http://www.rcees.cas.cn/zxjs/yszl/201112/t20111212_3411320.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Xu then worked at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] after its establishment in 1950.<ref name=":0" /> In 1975, the Institute of Environmental Chemistry of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] was established. She then began to engage in the analysis and research of environmental organic pollutants. From 1980 to 1982, Xu was a visiting scholar at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and later served as a visiting professor at the [[University of California, San Francisco]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://yswk.las.ac.cn/qiantai/Shouye_zhanshi.action?id=1995B09|title=中国科学院院士文库|website=yswk.las.ac.cn|access-date=2020-04-05}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/3373/2016-08/142922.shtml|title=简介|website=www.mmcs.org.cn|access-date=2020-04-05|archive-date=2020-03-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200301045847/http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/3373/2016-08/142922.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1995, she was elected as an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.rcees.cas.cn/au/hy/200907/t20090706_20945.html|title=History----Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences|website=english.rcees.cas.cn|access-date=2020-04-04|archive-date=2020-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407052435/http://english.rcees.cas.cn/au/hy/200907/t20090706_20945.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> She died in Beijing on March 27, 2014, at the age of 87.<ref name=":1" />

== Scientific career and accomplishments ==
Xu Xiaobai early engaged in inorganic chemistry research focused on [[Fluorescent lamp]] materials and high-temperature [[Rare-earth element|rare-earth]] compounds.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> Since the mid-1970s, she has been mainly engaged in analytical chemistry and pollution chemistry. She focused on [[polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon]] and its derivatives.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> She won the first prize in the Natural Science Award of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.rcees.cas.cn/rh/as/201106/t20110629_72101.html|title=Achievements----Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences|website=english.rcees.cas.cn|access-date=2020-04-05|archive-date=2020-04-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200407052434/http://english.rcees.cas.cn/rh/as/201106/t20110629_72101.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
